title: Erdos #1165: Favourite Sites of Planar Random Walks

problemStatement.formal: For a planar random walk, determine P(|F(n)| = r infinitely often) for r >= 3, where F(n) is the set of sites with maximal visit count at time n.
problemStatement.plain: How often can a two-dimensional random walk have exactly r favourite sites tied for the most visits?
whyMatters: Favourite-site questions probe the fine local-time structure of recurrent planar random walks.
Toth proved four or more favourite sites occur only finitely often, while Hao-Li-Okada-Zheng proved three occur infinitely often almost surely.
The Lean file records the resolution through a deliberately axiomatized random-walk/probability interface.

proven: Lean defines the Z^2 state space, a favourite-site count interface, and the probability of infinitely-often favourite-count events.
The complete resolution theorem is derived from the Toth upper-bound axiom and the Hao-Li-Okada-Zheng three-favourite-sites axiom.
Derived corollaries cover finite occurrence for r >= 4 and probability one for r = 3.
open: VisitCount, FavouriteSites, and prob_favourite_count_io are axiomatized interfaces rather than a full random-walk probability model.
The Toth and Hao-Li-Okada-Zheng theorems are active axioms, not Lean-derived probability proofs.
MaxVisitCount is a placeholder over the origin visit count, so metadata should not call it a true formal maximum.
knownResults.goal: Present the solved mathematical status while being explicit that Lean only derives the final consequences from axiomatized random-walk inputs.

currentState.focus: Metadata now supplies the missing favourite-sites statement and keeps the five active axioms separate from the derived resolution theorems.
blockers: The random-walk process, event probabilities, and two published favourite-site results are axiomatized.
currentState.nextAction: Future proof work would replace the placeholder random-walk interface with a real probability-space/local-time model.
